Location: Delcambre Canal Bridge, Delcambre (Delcambre Canal, off the GIWW near Intracoastal City)
Item: Delcambre Canal Bridge closed to boats – mechanical and electrical problems
Details: A Coast Guard broadcast notice (Sector New Orleans BNM 0606-26, posted Oct 26) says the Delcambre Canal Bridge is closed to marine traffic because of mechanical and electrical issues. Why it matters: boats that need an opening can't get up or down the canal to Delcambre's docks and shrimp-boat harbor until it's fixed.
When: Posted Oct 26 2026; no reopening date given
Notes: What to do: if you're headed up the Delcambre Canal, call Coast Guard Sector New Orleans or listen for broadcast notices on VHF 16 before committing – the notice gives no reopening time, contact number or alternate route. Uncertain: start date shown is the posting date, not a confirmed start.

Location: Mobile River, Mobile Bay and the Gulf off Alabama – SS United States tow route
Item: Moving Coast Guard safety zone around the SS United States tow, Nov 6–16
Details: The Coast Guard has set a 100-yard moving safety zone around the ocean liner SS United States and every tug towing it, from Pier 4 on the Mobile River down Mobile Bay and into the Gulf, out to 12 nm. Departure from Mobile is expected Nov 9; the ship is to be sunk as a reef about 22 nm southwest of Destin on Nov 12. Why it matters: a 990-ft dead-ship tow moving down the main ship channel will take up the channel and have little room to maneuver – small boats and sailboats tacking across the bay need to stay well clear.
When: Rule in force Nov 6–16 2026, enforced only while the tow is moving; expected departure Nov 9
Notes: What to do: listen on VHF 16 for the Coast Guard broadcast that gives the exact tow times; don't enter the 100-yard zone without permission (COTP Mobile on VHF 16 or (251) 266-5888). Departure date is the Coast Guard's 'anticipated' date and could slip with weather. Map point is the Mobile River at downtown Mobile. See also today's On the Water row for the Nov 12 sinking off Destin.

Location: Lake Okeechobee north shore – S-135 (J&S Fish Camp), G-36 (Henry Creek), S-127 (Buckhead Ridge), S-131 (Lakeport)
Item: UPDATE: Lake Okeechobee north-shore boat locks open every day again
Details: South Florida Water Management District says the north-shore boat locks that were closed for low water reopened starting Oct 28 and are open every day: S-135 5:30am–8:30pm; G-36, S-127 and S-131 5:30am–8pm. S-193 at Taylor Creek has been open daily since Oct 12, 5:30am–9pm. Why it matters: the rim-canal shortcuts into Okeechobee town, Buckhead Ridge and Lakeport are usable again – the restriction we flagged on Oct 19 is lifted.
Notes: What to do: lock tender (Advanced Lock Tender Division) 863-532-8042; check hours before arriving late in the day. These are SFWMD locks – the Corps' Okeechobee Waterway locks (863-983-8101) are separate, and the Point Chosen swing bridge on Route 2 still has an 8 ft clearance limit through Dec 22. Map point is a representative north-shore location.

Location: Gulf of Mexico about 22 nm southwest of Destin–Fort Walton Beach (Okaloosa County reef site)
Item: SS United States to be sunk as the world's largest artificial reef
Details: Okaloosa County plans to sink the 1952 ocean liner SS United States at about 10am Thu Nov 12, weather permitting, about 22 nm southwest of Destin. A public sendoff is planned Nov 11 at the Destin–Fort Walton Beach Convention Center, and Destin plans a live stream. Why it matters: once-in-a-lifetime sight; hundreds of private boats are expected offshore, so Destin Pass and the harbor will be busy.
When: Sinking Thu Nov 12 2026, ~10am (weather permitting); sendoff Wed Nov 11
Notes: What to do: if you go out, stay outside the restricted area – reports say the Coast Guard advises staying at least 1 nm from the hull until it's down; listen on VHF 16 for broadcasts. It's a 22-nm run offshore in November – check the sea state. No backup date announced. Map point is approximate (22 nm SW of Destin). Ties to today's ICW Alert row on the tow out of Mobile.

Location: Davis Island Yacht Club, 1315 Severn Ave, Tampa (Hillsborough Bay)
Item: Sailing Sisters Regatta – women's pursuit and buoy racing
Details: A one-day women's regatta at Davis Island Yacht Club with a distance (pursuit) race and drop-mark racing on Hillsborough Bay. Why it matters: a friendly way to watch – or join – women's racing in Tampa, on the same day the A-Class Catamaran Worlds start at the same club.
Notes: What to do: registration is open on Regatta Network; spectators can watch from the Davis Islands waterfront. Classes and whether it's women skippers only or whole crews weren't stated – check the Notice of Race. Same weekend as the A-Class Worlds (DIYC, Nov 7–14) and the U.S. Windsurfer Nationals in Clearwater (Nov 6–8).

Details: Seafood festival in riverfront Ormond Beach on the Halifax River stretch of the Atlantic ICW. Why it matters: an easy stop for southbound snowbirds coming down the ICW in late November.
Notes: What to do: confirm dates and venue with the organizer before planning a stop – this is from a festival calendar, and the exact venue wasn't confirmed. Map point is Ormond Beach town center. Same weekend as the Egmont Key Race on the Gulf side.

Location: Rigolets Pass – CSX railroad drawbridge near Slidell (Lake Pontchartrain to Lake Borgne / Mississippi Sound)
Item: Rigolets CSX rail bridge daytime closures scheduled to end Oct 31
Details: Since mid-August the CSX railroad drawbridge across the Rigolets has been closed to boats Monday–Saturday 8:30am–noon and 1:15–4:45pm while PCL Construction works on it (Coast Guard Sector New Orleans BNM 0468-26). That notice says the work runs until Oct 31, 2026. Why it matters: the Rigolets is the main way between Lake Pontchartrain and Lake Borgne / Mississippi Sound, and sailboats that need the bridge to open have had to plan around two long daytime closures six days a week.
When: Closure window Aug 2026 – Oct 31 2026 (reopening not yet confirmed)
Notes: What to do: before relying on normal openings on Mon Nov 2, call the bridge tender (the notice says to contact the tender for schedule updates) or listen for Coast Guard broadcast notices on VHF 16. Keep to no-wake through the work area. Uncertain: no follow-up notice confirming the work finished or was extended was found today, and a Waterway Guide alert lists the closure as 'not active' with no date – treat Oct 31 as the scheduled end, not a confirmed reopening.

Location: Texas City Channel at Docks 42/43, about 1 nm southwest of Texas City Channel Light 21 (Galveston Bay)
Item: Monopile driving in Texas City Channel – weekday traffic limits through about Feb 2027
Details: Coast Guard Vessel Traffic Service Houston-Galveston says monopile driving at Texas City Docks 42/43 resumes Mon Nov 2 and runs weekdays: 7–10am and noon–4pm no ship traffic and single-barge tows only; 10am–noon normal traffic. The work is projected to continue through February 2027. Why it matters: the work barge can reach to mid-channel, so the Texas City Channel is narrowed during work hours – sailboats heading in or out of Texas City should expect a crowded, constricted channel and tows waiting for their window.
When: Weekdays 7am–4pm (open 10am–noon), from Nov 2 2026 through about Feb 2027
Notes: What to do: give the work site a wide berth and pass at slow speed; the RUSSELL MARINE 1 stands by on VHF 13 and 87A (boat phone 281-979-4696), and VTS Houston-Galveston answers 24/7 at 281-464-4837. The traffic measures are written for ships and tows – no specific rule for recreational boats was given. End date is the Coast Guard's 'projected' date. Map point is approximate.

Location: Vermilion River, Mile 50 to Mile 0 (crosses the GIWW near Intracoastal City)
Item: Corps debris-removal crews on the Vermilion River through June 2027
Details: A U.S. Army Corps of Engineers maintenance unit (New Orleans District notice MVN 26-104) is clearing debris on the Vermilion River from Mile 50 down to Mile 0, seven days a week in daylight, from about Oct 23, 2026 to about June 1, 2027. Why it matters: boats running the Vermilion up toward Abbeville or crossing it at the GIWW will meet work boats in the channel and should expect to slow down and make passing arrangements.
When: Daylight, 7 days a week, Oct 23 2026 – about Jun 1 2027
Notes: What to do: call the maintenance unit on VHF 13 for passing arrangements and transit at your slowest safe speed. Dates are 'approximately' in the notice. Map point is the river near its GIWW crossing at Intracoastal City (representative). Nearby: Leland Bowman Lock (GIWW) had long queues as of Oct 27 – see the Oct 28 row.

Location: Key West – Truman Waterfront and the Outer Mole (Key West harbor race course)
Item: Key West World Championship powerboat races – race days Nov 4, 6 and 8
Details: The Race World Offshore Key West World Championship runs Nov 1–8, 2026, with racing on Wed Nov 4, Fri Nov 6 and Sun Nov 8 from 10am on a harbor course you can watch from shore. The race boats parade down Duval Street on trailers Sun Nov 1 around 4pm, and the dry pits at Truman Waterfront are free all week. Why it matters: a great show if you're in Key West – but on race days the harbor course is off-limits, so moving a boat in or out of Key West harbor takes planning.
When: Nov 1–8 2026; races Wed Nov 4, Fri Nov 6, Sun Nov 8 from 10am
Notes: What to do: plan arrivals and departures for non-race days; on race days listen on VHF 16 for Coast Guard Sector Key West broadcasts on the closed race area. Viewing: the Outer Mole is about $25 per race day (kids and military free); Mallory Square is free. No 2026 Coast Guard enforcement notice was found today – the race area is a standing Coast Guard regulated area (33 CFR 100.701), but exact 2026 hours aren't confirmed. Key West marinas get busy this week.
